thread:
maria (Support): FYI customer reports spikes of 502/504s from hosted inference around 12:10 UTC, started ~12:08. They see timeouts when calling /v1/generate. Request ids: req_8a3f, req_8a40.
kevin-oncall: digging in — can you paste a sample request id and any client side trace?
maria (Support): pasted one: req_8a3f. Customer says it started right after we rolled the memcached auth keys earlier. They saw a bunch of 5xx gateway errors.
dash-deploy-bot: deploy:auth-rotation v2.14 rolled at 12:05 UTC by infra/rotate-keys.
noah (Eng Runtime): seeing gateway 502s from api-gateway: "upstream prematurely closed connection" and memcached connection refusals in runtime logs. Suspect cache auth rotation + warmup causing thundering retries.
elaine (Eng Infra): metrics: memcached connection_open errors spike at 12:07-12:09, pool exhaustion on cluster memcache-prod-1. Also noticed increased RTOs between edge and memcached.
amina (SRE): stack traces show transient auth failure followed by many clients failing open -> gateway returns 502. Sample from runtime logs: ```
2026-03-17T12:08:13Z runtime ERROR cache_client: auth failed for server memcache-prod-1:11211 -> "AUTH_FAILED"
2026-03-17T12:08:14Z runtime WARN  cache_fetch: pool exhausted, rejecting request -> fallback=false
2026-03-17T12:08:14Z gateway ERROR upstream returned 502 for req req_8a3f
```
maria (Support): customer repro steps: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"rwd-small","prompt":"hello"}' -> ~10% requests 502/504 during window. They captured latency traces.
kevin-oncall: immediate mitigation: can infra flip cache fallback to permissive (allow bypass) for hosted-prod while we stabilize auth rotation? Helps avoid 5xx at cost of increased model cost.
elaine (Eng Infra): I can enable cache-bypass for the gateway route in ~2min. Command: `infra toggle route.hosted.cache_bypass --env=prod --route=/v1/generate --value=on`
noah (Eng Runtime): also recommend increasing client auth retry backoff and enable soft-fail to origin (treat cache misses as misses, not hard errors). We'll patch runtime but that's not instant.
amina (SRE): applied bypass -> observing immediate drop in 5xx from 12:12. Errors from 12%->0.6% in 2m. Keeping monitoring.
henry (Customer Success): I messaged the customer: told them we're rolling mitigations and will follow up with timeline. Offered credits for the disruption.
maria (Support): recording repro + notes: likely root cause = auth key rotation on memcached cluster triggered mass reconnects + warm cache evictions (hot prefix), leading to pool exhaustion and gateway 502s. Also saw many clients not falling back gracefully.
noah (Eng Runtime): follow-ups: 1) make cache client soft-fail by default for hosted API (config flag), 2) improve auth rotation handshake (grace period), 3) add leader warming to avoid prefix eviction storms. I'll open runtime PRs.
elaine (Eng Infra): infra follow-ups: roll memcached auth rotation procedure to staggered keys, add health-check gating before removing old keys. Also we should add a short read-only fallback cluster for rotations.
amina (SRE): postmortem note: label as sev3 (customer impacting, mitigated). Will capture timeline and metrics.
maria (Support): closing loop with customer at 12:20 UTC — they confirm latency and 5xx normalized. Keeping thread open for follow-up action items. :thumbsup:
kevin-oncall: nice work. Add runbook step: "if auth rotation + memcached spike => enable cache_bypass, monitor memcache pool, rollback rotation if failures persist"
maria (Support): filing support ticket with all logs + links to runbook and follow-ups.
